title: If you weren't so stubborn …
titleHi: अगर तुम इतनी ज़िद्दी न होतीं …
scope: Conditionals (2): a perfective verb in the अगर clause for a supposition (अगर राम आया तो …); unfulfilled conditions with the imperfective participle and no auxiliary in both clauses (feminine plural nasalized, अगर often dropped); past counterfactuals with perfective participle + होता (बुलाया होता); हालाँकि … फिर भी / तो भी “although … even so”, formal यद्यपि … तथापि; compound verbs (2) with डालना (vigour), बैठना (foolishness), पड़ना (suddenness), उठना (inception), रखना (firmness), taking ने only when both verbs do; registers of vocabulary: Perso-Arabic and Sanskritic synonyms

items.q: Fill the gap: “If it rains, we will stay at home (lit. “… then … only”).”
items.hi: अगर बारिश ___ तो हम घर पर ही रहेंगे ।
items.say: अगर बारिश हुई तो हम घर पर ही रहेंगे ।
items.en: If[0] it rains[1+2], we[4] {will stay}[8] at home[5+6] (lit. “… then[3] … only[7]”).
wrong: हुईं is plural. बारिश is singular.
items.why: A perfective verb in the अगर clause makes the condition a given, a supposition: अगर मोहन आया तो … “supposing Mohan comes …”.

items.q: Fill the gap: “If I had the money, I would buy a new car (lit. “… then …”). (a man speaking)”
items.hi: अगर मेरे पास पैसे ___ तो मैं नई गाड़ी ख़रीदता ।
items.say: अगर मेरे पास पैसे होते तो मैं नई गाड़ी ख़रीदता ।
items.en: If[0] I[1+2] had[4] the money[3], I[6] {would buy}[9] a new[7] car[8] (lit. “… then[5] …”). (a man speaking)
wrong: होंगे is future, an open condition. ख़रीदता shows the condition is hypothetical, so the imperfective participle alone — होते.
हैं is present, an open condition. A hypothetical condition takes होते, with no auxiliary.
Not a word. The hypothetical is होते, with nothing added.
items.why: An unfulfilled, hypothetical condition uses the imperfective participle without an auxiliary in both clauses (अगर मैं कवि होता तो … लिखता). The feminine plural is nasalized. अगर is often dropped.

items.q: Fill the gap: “If he worked hard, he'd pass (lit. “… then …”).”
items.hi: अगर वह मेहनत करता तो पास हो ___ ।
items.say: अगर वह मेहनत करता तो पास हो जाता ।
items.en: If[0] he[1] worked hard[2+3], he'd pass[5+6+7] (lit. “… then[4] …”).
wrong: जाएगा is future. With an unfulfilled condition both clauses take the imperfective participle alone — जाता.
गया states a fact. The condition is hypothetical — जाता.
Not a word. The hypothetical is जाता, with nothing added.
items.why: An unfulfilled, hypothetical condition uses the imperfective participle without an auxiliary in both clauses (अगर मैं कवि होता तो … लिखता). The feminine plural is nasalized. अगर is often dropped.

items.q: Fill the gap: “If the girls had come on time, we wouldn't have missed our train (lit. “… then …”).”
items.hi: अगर लड़कियाँ समय पर ___ तो हमारी गाड़ी नहीं छूटती ।
items.say: अगर लड़कियाँ समय पर आतीं तो हमारी गाड़ी नहीं छूटती ।
items.en: If[0] the girls[1] {had come}[4] on time[2+3], we {wouldn't have missed}[8+9] our[6] train[7] (lit. “… then[5] …”).
wrong: The feminine plural is nasalized — आतीं.
आते is masculine. लड़कियाँ is feminine.
items.why: An unfulfilled, hypothetical condition uses the imperfective participle without an auxiliary in both clauses (अगर मैं कवि होता तो … लिखता). The feminine plural is nasalized. अगर is often dropped.

items.q: Fill the gap: “If we had set out early in the morning, we'd have arrived on time (lit. “… then …”).”
items.hi: अगर हम सुबह जल्दी निकले ___ तो समय पर पहुँच जाते ।
items.say: अगर हम सुबह जल्दी निकले होते तो समय पर पहुँच जाते ।
items.en: If[0] we[1] {had set out}[4+5] early[3] in the morning[2], we'd {have arrived}[9+10] on time[7+8] (lit. “… then[6] …”).
wrong: निकले थे is a plain past fact. A past unfulfilled condition takes the perfective participle + होता — निकले होते.
हैं would make it present. A past unfulfilled condition takes निकले होते.
items.why: For an unfulfilled condition in the past, the अगर clause can take the perfective participle + होता (बुलाया होता), and the other clause usually has the imperfective participle alone.

items.q: What does this sentence mean?
items.hi: अगर पापा यहाँ होते तो बहुत ख़ुश होते ।
items.a: If Papa were here, he'd be very happy.
wrong: Papa is here and he's very happy.
होते without an auxiliary is hypothetical: he isn't here.
When Papa comes, he'll be very happy.
That would be जब … तब with future verbs.
items.why: An unfulfilled, hypothetical condition uses the imperfective participle without an auxiliary in both clauses (अगर मैं कवि होता तो … लिखता). The feminine plural is nasalized. अगर is often dropped.

items.q: What does this sentence mean?
items.hi: तुम थोड़ा पहले आते तो खाना गरम मिलता ।
items.a: If you'd come a bit earlier, you'd have got your food hot.
wrong: You came early, so the food was hot.
आते and मिलता without auxiliaries are hypothetical: you didn't come early.
Come a bit earlier and the food will be hot.
That would be a command and a future: पहले आओ, खाना गरम मिलेगा.
items.why: An unfulfilled, hypothetical condition uses the imperfective participle without an auxiliary in both clauses (अगर मैं कवि होता तो … लिखता). The feminine plural is nasalized. अगर is often dropped.

items.q: Fill the gap: “If the train arrives on time, we will go straight to the hotel (lit. “… then …”).”
items.hi: अगर गाड़ी समय पर ___ तो हम सीधे होटल जाएँगे ।
items.say: अगर गाड़ी समय पर पहुँची तो हम सीधे होटल जाएँगे ।
items.en: If[0] the train[1] arrives[4] on time[2+3], we[6] {will go}[9] straight[7] to the hotel[8] (lit. “… then[5] …”).
wrong: पहुँचीं is plural. It is one train.
items.why: A perfective verb in the अगर clause makes the condition a given, a supposition: अगर मोहन आया तो … “supposing Mohan comes …”.

items.q: Which sentence is a hypothetical (unfulfilled) condition?
items.a: अगर वह यहाँ होता तो मदद करता ।
wrong: अगर वह यहाँ है तो मदद करेगा ।
This is an open condition: he may well be here.
अगर वह यहाँ आया तो मदद करेगा ।
This is a supposition: “if he comes”.
items.why: An unfulfilled, hypothetical condition uses the imperfective participle without an auxiliary in both clauses (अगर मैं कवि होता तो … लिखता). The feminine plural is nasalized. अगर is often dropped.
items.say: अगर वह यहाँ होता तो मदद करता ।
items.en: If[0] he[1] were[3] here[2], he'd help[5+6] (lit. “… then[4] …”).

items.q: Fill the gap: “If I'd known, I would have come too (lit. “… then …”). (a man speaking)”
items.hi: अगर मुझे पता होता तो मैं भी ___ ।
items.say: अगर मुझे पता होता तो मैं भी आता ।
items.en: If[0] I'd[1] known[2+3], I[5] {would have come}[7] too[6] (lit. “… then[4] …”). (a man speaking)
wrong: आऊँगा is future. With an unfulfilled condition the other clause takes the imperfective participle alone — आता.
आया states what happened. The condition is hypothetical — आता.
items.why: An unfulfilled, hypothetical condition uses the imperfective participle without an auxiliary in both clauses (अगर मैं कवि होता तो … लिखता). The feminine plural is nasalized. अगर is often dropped.

items.q: Fill the gap: “If Mother were here, everything would be all right (lit. “… then …”).”
items.hi: अगर माँ यहाँ होतीं तो सब कुछ ठीक ___ ।
items.say: अगर माँ यहाँ होतीं तो सब कुछ ठीक होता ।
items.en: If[0] Mother[1] were[3] here[2], everything[5+6] {would be}[8] all right[7] (lit. “… then[4] …”).
wrong: होगा is future. With an unfulfilled condition the other clause takes the imperfective participle alone — होता.
हुआ states what happened. The condition is hypothetical — होता.
items.why: An unfulfilled, hypothetical condition uses the imperfective participle without an auxiliary in both clauses (अगर मैं कवि होता तो … लिखता). The feminine plural is nasalized. अगर is often dropped.

items.q: What does this sentence mean?
items.hi: अगर उसने मेरी बात सुनी होती तो यह सब न होता ।
items.a: If he'd listened to me, none of this would have happened.
wrong: He listened to me, so none of this happened.
सुनी होती … न होता is counterfactual: he didn't listen.
If he listens to me, none of this will happen.
That would be future: सुनेगा … नहीं होगा.
items.why: For an unfulfilled condition in the past, the अगर clause can take the perfective participle + होता (बुलाया होता), and the other clause usually has the imperfective participle alone.

items.q: Fill the gap: “Although he was ill, he still went to the office.”
items.hi: ___ वह बीमार था, फिर भी वह दफ़्तर गया ।
items.say: हालाँकि वह बीमार था, फिर भी वह दफ़्तर गया ।
items.en: Although[0] he[1] was[3] ill[2], he[6] still[4+5] went[8] to the office[7].
wrong: Not a word. The spelling is हालाँकि.
items.why: हालाँकि “although” opens the first clause, and फिर भी or तो भी “even so” the second. Formal Hindi uses यद्यपि … तथापि.

items.q: Fill the gap: “Although this work is difficult, we'll do it all the same.”
items.hi: हालाँकि यह काम मुश्किल है, ___ भी हम इसे करेंगे ।
items.say: हालाँकि यह काम मुश्किल है, फिर भी हम इसे करेंगे ।
items.en: Although[0] this[1] work[2] is[4] difficult[3], we'll[7] do[9] it[8] {all the same}[5+6].
wrong: कभी भी is “ever, at any time”.
items.why: हालाँकि “although” opens the first clause, and फिर भी or तो भी “even so” the second. Formal Hindi uses यद्यपि … तथापि.

items.q: Fill the gap: “Although Mohan's plan was good, nevertheless it did not succeed.”
items.hi: ___ मोहन की योजना अच्छी थी, तथापि वह सफल नहीं हुई ।
items.say: यद्यपि मोहन की योजना अच्छी थी, तथापि वह सफल नहीं हुई ।
items.en: Although[0] Mohan's[1+2] plan[3] was[5] good[4], {nevertheless}[6] it[7] {did not}[9] succeed[8+10].
wrong: यदि is “if”. The formal “although” is यद्यपि.
तथापि is “nevertheless”, which opens the second clause.
Not a word. The spelling is यद्यपि.
items.why: हालाँकि “although” opens the first clause, and फिर भी or तो भी “even so” the second. Formal Hindi uses यद्यपि … तथापि.

items.q: Fill the gap: “Although the journey was long, nevertheless nobody was put to any trouble.”
items.hi: यद्यपि यात्रा लंबी थी, ___ किसी को कष्ट नहीं हुआ ।
items.say: यद्यपि यात्रा लंबी थी, तथापि किसी को कष्ट नहीं हुआ ।
items.en: Although[0] the journey[1] was[3] long[2], {nevertheless}[4] nobody[5+6+8] {was put to}[9] any trouble[7].
wrong: यद्यपि opens the first clause. The second clause takes तथापि.
हालाँकि opens the first clause. The second clause takes तथापि (or फिर भी).
items.why: हालाँकि “although” opens the first clause, and फिर भी or तो भी “even so” the second. Formal Hindi uses यद्यपि … तथापि.

items.q: What does this sentence mean?
items.hi: हालाँकि सीता अमीर नहीं है, फिर भी वह सबकी मदद करती है ।
items.a: Although Sita isn't rich, she still helps everyone.
wrong: Because Sita isn't rich, she helps everyone.
Sita is rich, so she helps everyone.
नहीं है — she is not rich.
items.why: हालाँकि “although” opens the first clause, and फिर भी or तो भी “even so” the second. Formal Hindi uses यद्यपि … तथापि.

items.q: Which is the formal, Sanskritic way to say “although … even so”?
items.why: हालाँकि “although” opens the first clause, and फिर भी or तो भी “even so” the second. Formal Hindi uses यद्यपि … तथापि.

items.q: What does this sentence mean?
items.hi: हालाँकि घड़ी पुरानी है, तो भी ठीक चलती है ।
items.a: Although the watch is old, it still keeps good time.
wrong: Because the watch is old, it doesn't keep good time.
हालाँकि is “although”, and ठीक चलती है is “keeps good time”.
The watch is new, but it doesn't keep good time.
पुरानी is “old”, and ठीक चलती है is positive.
items.why: हालाँकि “although” opens the first clause, and फिर भी or तो भी “even so” the second. Formal Hindi uses यद्यपि … तथापि.

items.q: Fill the gap: “Although it had got very late, the children went on playing all the same.”
items.hi: हालाँकि रात बहुत हो गई थी, तो ___ बच्चे खेलते रहे ।
items.say: हालाँकि रात बहुत हो गई थी, तो भी बच्चे खेलते रहे ।
items.en: Although[0] it {had got}[3+4+5] very[2] late[1], the children[8] {went on}[10] playing[9] {all the same}[6+7].
wrong: तो ही is not used here. “Even so” is तो भी (or फिर भी).
तो तक is not a phrase. “Even so” is तो भी.
items.why: हालाँकि “although” opens the first clause, and फिर भी or तो भी “even so” the second. Formal Hindi uses यद्यपि … तथापि.

lessons.title: कर बैठना, रो पड़ना
lessons.desc: Compound verbs with डालना, बैठना, पड़ना, उठना, रखना

items.q: Fill the gap: “The children gobbled up all the mangoes.”
items.hi: बच्चों ने सारे आम खा ___ ।
items.say: बच्चों ने सारे आम खा डाले ।
items.en: The children[0+1] {gobbled up}[4+5] all[2] the mangoes[3].
wrong: डाला is singular. With ने the verb agrees with आम, here plural — खा डाले.
डालीं is feminine. आम is masculine.
Not a word. डालना has a consonant stem: डाला, डाले, with no -y-.
items.why: डालना as an auxiliary: an action done vigorously, decisively, violently or recklessly (फाड़ डालना, मार डालना, पी डालना). A compound verb takes ने only when both the main verb and the auxiliary take ने.

items.q: Fill the gap: “Raj went and quarrelled with his boss in anger.”
items.hi: ___ गुस्से में अपने मालिक से लड़ बैठा ।
items.say: राज गुस्से में अपने मालिक से लड़ बैठा ।
items.en: Raj[0] {went and quarrelled}[6+7] with[5] his[3] boss[4] in anger[1+2].
wrong: लड़ना and बैठना don't take ने, so the compound doesn't either.
The subject of लड़ बैठा is a plain राज.
Not a word. बैठना has a consonant stem: बैठा, with no -y-.
items.why: बैठना as an auxiliary: an action done foolishly or stubbornly (कर बैठना “go and do”). बैठना never takes ने, so the compound doesn't either.

items.q: Fill the gap: “Seeing the end of the film, the children burst into tears.”
items.hi: फ़िल्म का अंत देखकर बच्चे रो ___ ।
items.say: फ़िल्म का अंत देखकर बच्चे रो पड़े ।
items.en: Seeing[3] the end[2] of the film[0+1], the children[4] {burst into tears}[5+6].
wrong: पड़ा is singular. बच्चे is plural.
Bursting into tears is रो पड़ना. डालना is for vigorous action on something.
Not a word. पड़ना has a consonant stem: पड़ा, पड़े, with no -y-.
items.why: पड़ना as an auxiliary: suddenness or a change of state, sometimes downward movement (रो पड़ना “burst into tears”, उतर पड़ना).

items.q: Fill the gap: “Seeing the fire, people rushed out of their houses.”
items.hi: आग देखकर लोग घरों से बाहर निकल ___ ।
items.say: आग देखकर लोग घरों से बाहर निकल पड़े ।
items.en: Seeing[1] the fire[0], people[2] rushed[6+7] out[5] of their houses[3+4].
wrong: पड़ा is singular. लोग is plural.
बैठना suggests something foolish, “went and did”. A sudden rush is निकल पड़ना.
items.why: पड़ना as an auxiliary: suddenness or a change of state, sometimes downward movement (रो पड़ना “burst into tears”, उतर पड़ना).

items.q: Fill the gap: “He cried out in fear.”
items.hi: डर से वह चिल्ला ___ ।
items.say: डर से वह चिल्ला उठा ।
items.en: He[2] {cried out}[3+4] in fear[0+1].
wrong: उठी is feminine. The cue says “he”.
चिल्लाना is intransitive. A sudden outburst is चिल्ला उठना.
Not a word. उठना has a consonant stem: उठा, with no -y-.
items.why: उठना as an auxiliary: the start of an action or feeling, sometimes upward movement (बिगड़ उठना “flare up”, जल उठना “burst into flames”).

items.q: Fill the gap: “I have made food for you (and it's ready).”
items.hi: मैंने तुम्हारे लिए खाना बना ___ है ।
items.say: मैंने तुम्हारे लिए खाना बना रखा है ।
items.en: I[0] {have made}[4+5+6] food[3] for[2] you[1] (and it's ready).
wrong: रखी is feminine. With ने the verb agrees with खाना, masculine.
रखे is plural. खाना is singular.
Not a word. रखना has a consonant stem: रखा, with no -y-.
items.why: रखना as an auxiliary: firmness, or a result that lasts (देख रखा है “have seen and have my eye on”). A compound verb takes ने only when both the main verb and the auxiliary take ने.

items.q: Fill the gap: “Mother has bought sweets for the guests (and has them ready).”
items.hi: माँ ने मेहमानों के लिए मिठाइयाँ ख़रीद ___ हैं ।
items.say: माँ ने मेहमानों के लिए मिठाइयाँ ख़रीद रखी हैं ।
items.en: Mother[0+1] {has bought}[6+7+8] sweets[5] for[3+4] the guests[2] (and has them ready).
wrong: With ने the verb agrees with मिठाइयाँ, feminine plural — ख़रीद रखी हैं.
The nasal goes on the last word only — रखी हैं.
items.why: रखना as an auxiliary: firmness, or a result that lasts (देख रखा है “have seen and have my eye on”). A compound verb takes ने only when both the main verb and the auxiliary take ने.

items.q: What does this sentence mean?
items.hi: डाकुओं ने पूरे गाँव को लूट डाला ।
items.a: The bandits looted the whole village.
wrong: The bandits were robbed by the village.
The bandits tried to loot the whole village.
लूट डाला is done, and done ruthlessly: no “tried”.
items.why: डालना as an auxiliary: an action done vigorously, decisively, violently or recklessly (फाड़ डालना, मार डालना, पी डालना). A compound verb takes ने only when both the main verb and the auxiliary take ने.

items.q: Which is right for “Raj went and made a mistake”?
wrong: A compound verb takes ने only if both verbs take ने. बैठना doesn't.
बैठना doesn't take ने, so the verb agrees with राज — कर बैठा.
items.why: बैठना as an auxiliary: an action done foolishly or stubbornly (कर बैठना “go and do”). बैठना never takes ने, so the compound doesn't either.
items.say: राज ग़लती कर बैठा ।
items.en: Raj[0] {went and made}[2+3] a mistake[1].

items.q: Fill the gap: “Someone smashed all the windows of the shop.”
items.hi: किसी ने दुकान की सारी खिड़कियाँ तोड़ ___ ।
items.say: किसी ने दुकान की सारी खिड़कियाँ तोड़ डालीं ।
items.en: Someone[0+1] smashed[6+7] all[4] the windows[5] of the shop[2+3].
wrong: With ने the verb agrees with खिड़कियाँ, feminine plural.
डाली is singular. खिड़कियाँ is plural, and the nasal goes on the last word — डालीं.
items.why: डालना as an auxiliary: an action done vigorously, decisively, violently or recklessly (फाड़ डालना, मार डालना, पी डालना). A compound verb takes ने only when both the main verb and the auxiliary take ने.

items.q: What does this sentence mean?
items.hi: पुलिस ने चोरों को पकड़ रखा है ।
items.a: The police are holding the thieves.
wrong: The police are trying to catch the thieves.
पकड़ रखा है is done and lasting: they have them.
The thieves have caught the police.
items.why: रखना as an auxiliary: firmness, or a result that lasts (देख रखा है “have seen and have my eye on”). A compound verb takes ने only when both the main verb and the auxiliary take ने.

items.q: Which auxiliary suggests doing something foolishly?
wrong: उठना suggests the start of an action or feeling.
रखना suggests firmness or a lasting result.
items.why: बैठना as an auxiliary: an action done foolishly or stubbornly (कर बैठना “go and do”). बैठना never takes ने, so the compound doesn't either.

items.q: Fill the gap: “Someone killed that poor dog.”
items.hi: किसी ने उस बेचारे कुत्ते को मार ___ ।
items.say: किसी ने उस बेचारे कुत्ते को मार डाला ।
items.en: Someone[0+1] killed[6+7] that[2] poor[3] dog[4+5].
wrong: With को on the object the verb is masculine singular — मार डाला.
बैठना doesn't take ने, so किसी ने … मार बैठा is impossible.
items.why: डालना as an auxiliary: an action done vigorously, decisively, violently or recklessly (फाड़ डालना, मार डालना, पी डालना). A compound verb takes ने only when both the main verb and the auxiliary take ने.

items.q: What does this sentence mean?
items.hi: मैंने कुछ पैसे बचा रखे हैं ।
wrong: बचा रखे हैं is “have saved and kept”.
I need to save some money.
रखे हैं is done: the money is already saved.
items.why: रखना as an auxiliary: firmness, or a result that lasts (देख रखा है “have seen and have my eye on”). A compound verb takes ने only when both the main verb and the auxiliary take ने.

items.q: Which is the formal, Sanskritic word for ख़त्म “finished”?
wrong: Not a word. The word is समाप्त.
items.why: Formal Hindi uses many Sanskrit loanwords, everyday Hindi a freer mix with many Perso-Arabic words: समाप्त / ख़त्म, प्रश्न / सवाल, वर्ष / साल, यात्रा / सफ़र, उत्तर / जवाब, आवश्यकता / ज़रूरत.

items.q: Which is the everyday, Perso-Arabic word for प्रश्न “question”?
items.why: Formal Hindi uses many Sanskrit loanwords, everyday Hindi a freer mix with many Perso-Arabic words: समाप्त / ख़त्म, प्रश्न / सवाल, वर्ष / साल, यात्रा / सफ़र, उत्तर / जवाब, आवश्यकता / ज़रूरत.

items.q: Which is the formal, Sanskritic word for साल “year”?
items.why: Formal Hindi uses many Sanskrit loanwords, everyday Hindi a freer mix with many Perso-Arabic words: समाप्त / ख़त्म, प्रश्न / सवाल, वर्ष / साल, यात्रा / सफ़र, उत्तर / जवाब, आवश्यकता / ज़रूरत.

items.q: Which is the everyday, Perso-Arabic word for यात्रा “journey”?
items.why: Formal Hindi uses many Sanskrit loanwords, everyday Hindi a freer mix with many Perso-Arabic words: समाप्त / ख़त्म, प्रश्न / सवाल, वर्ष / साल, यात्रा / सफ़र, उत्तर / जवाब, आवश्यकता / ज़रूरत.

items.q: Which is the formal, Sanskritic word for हफ़्ता “week”?
items.why: Formal Hindi uses many Sanskrit loanwords, everyday Hindi a freer mix with many Perso-Arabic words: समाप्त / ख़त्म, प्रश्न / सवाल, वर्ष / साल, यात्रा / सफ़र, उत्तर / जवाब, आवश्यकता / ज़रूरत.

items.q: Which is the everyday, Perso-Arabic word for उत्तर “reply”?
items.why: Formal Hindi uses many Sanskrit loanwords, everyday Hindi a freer mix with many Perso-Arabic words: समाप्त / ख़त्म, प्रश्न / सवाल, वर्ष / साल, यात्रा / सफ़र, उत्तर / जवाब, आवश्यकता / ज़रूरत.

items.q: Which sentence is in the more formal, Sanskritic style?
items.a: मुझे इस पुस्तक की आवश्यकता है ।
wrong: मुझे इस किताब की ज़रूरत है ।
This is everyday Hindi: किताब and ज़रूरत are Perso-Arabic.
This is everyday Hindi, with the Perso-Arabic किताब.
items.why: Formal Hindi uses many Sanskrit loanwords, everyday Hindi a freer mix with many Perso-Arabic words: समाप्त / ख़त्म, प्रश्न / सवाल, वर्ष / साल, यात्रा / सफ़र, उत्तर / जवाब, आवश्यकता / ज़रूरत.
items.say: मुझे इस पुस्तक की आवश्यकता है ।
items.en: I[0] need[3+4+5] this[1] book[2].

items.q: Which is the everyday word for कठिन “difficult”?
items.why: Formal Hindi uses many Sanskrit loanwords, everyday Hindi a freer mix with many Perso-Arabic words: समाप्त / ख़त्म, प्रश्न / सवाल, वर्ष / साल, यात्रा / सफ़र, उत्तर / जवाब, आवश्यकता / ज़रूरत.

items.q: Which word must be Sanskritic, judging by its letters?
wrong: The dotted kh of ख़ास shows a Persian origin.
The dotted q of क़ीमती shows a Persian origin.
items.why: Only Sanskrit loanwords contain the letters ṇ, ṣ, kṣ and jñ (as in विशेष). Only words from Persian contain the dotted q, kh and g.

items.q: Which is the formal word for “but”?
items.why: Formal Hindi uses many Sanskrit loanwords, everyday Hindi a freer mix with many Perso-Arabic words: समाप्त / ख़त्म, प्रश्न / सवाल, वर्ष / साल, यात्रा / सफ़र, उत्तर / जवाब, आवश्यकता / ज़रूरत.

items.en: If[0] I[1] were[3] rich[2], I'd travel[6] the world[5] (lit. “… then[4] …”). (a man speaking)
wrong: होगा is future. A hypothetical condition takes होता.
The other clause also takes the imperfective participle alone — घूमता.

items.en: If[0] he[1] {had taken}[3+4] the medicine[2], he[6] {would have got}[8+9] better[7] (lit. “… then[5] …”).
wrong: With ने the participle agrees with दवा, feminine — ली होती.
होता would agree with a masculine object. दवा is feminine — ली होती.

items.en: Although[0] it {had got}[2+3+4] late[1], he[7] came[8] {all the same}[5+6].
wrong: देर is feminine — हो गई थी.
Not a word. The spelling is हालाँकि.

items.en: Although[0] the work[1] was[3] difficult[2], {nevertheless}[4] we[5] finished[7+8] it[6].
wrong: With ने in the perfective — हमने.
Not a word. The spelling is यद्यपि.

items.en: The workers[0+1] {cut down}[4+5] all[2] the trees[3].
wrong: डाला is singular. The verb agrees with पेड़, here plural — काट डाले.
कटना is intransitive, “be cut”. With ने the transitive काटना is needed — काट.

items.en: Sita[0] {went and lost}[3+4] her[1] key[2].
wrong: बैठना doesn't take ने, so neither does the compound.
बैठा is masculine. The verb agrees with सीता.

items.en: Hearing[1] the noise[0], the child[2] {burst into tears}[3+4].
wrong: रोना and पड़ना don't take ने.
Bursting into tears is रो पड़ना.
Not a word. पड़ना has a consonant stem: पड़ा, with no -y-.

items.en: Suddenly[0] the crowd[1] {cried out}[2+3].
wrong: चिल्लाना and उठना don't take ने.

items.en: I[0] {have already}[2+3+5+6] told[4] him[1].
wrong: रखी is feminine. There's no feminine object here — बता रखा है.
बताना and रखना both take ने, so the compound does — मैंने.

items.en: If[0] the girls[1] were[3] here[2], they'd sing[5] (lit. “… then[4] …”).
wrong: The feminine plural is nasalized — होतीं.
गाते is masculine. लड़कियाँ is feminine — गातीं.

items.en: If[0] Mohan[1] comes[2], {ask him to sit down}[4+5] (lit. “… then[3] …”).
wrong: आई is feminine. मोहन is a man.
आता without an auxiliary would make it hypothetical, “if Mohan came”.

items.en: This[0] news[1] {will be published}[3+4] soon[2].
wrong: होगी is feminine. समाचार is masculine.
ख़बर is the everyday word, and feminine, so it doesn't fit होगा.

lessons.title: What does it mean?
lessons.desc: Read a sentence, pick the translation

items.q: What does this sentence mean?
items.hi: अगर मुझे छात्रवृत्ति मिल जाती तो मैं विदेश पढ़ने जाता ।
items.a: If I'd got the scholarship, I'd have gone abroad to study.
wrong: I got the scholarship and went abroad to study.
मिल जाती and जाता are hypothetical: it didn't happen.
If I get the scholarship, I'll go abroad to study.
That would be future: मिलेगी … जाऊँगा.

items.q: What does this sentence mean?
items.hi: हड़ताल के कारण आज कोई बस नहीं चल रही ।
items.a: Because of the strike no buses are running today.
wrong: The buses are running in spite of the strike.
There'll be a strike today because the buses aren't running.
It's the other way round: the strike stops the buses.

items.q: What does this sentence mean?
items.hi: इस दवा का असर बहुत जल्दी पड़ता है ।
items.a: This medicine takes effect very quickly.
wrong: This medicine has to be taken quickly.
असर पड़ना is “to have an effect”.

items.q: What does this sentence mean?
items.hi: दंगे में कई दुकानें जल गईं ।
items.a: Several shops burned down in the riot.
wrong: Several shops were looted in the riot.
जल गईं is “burned”. “Looted” would be लूटी गईं.
Several shops closed before the riot.

items.q: What does this sentence mean?
items.hi: हम सब इस योजना से सहमत हैं ।
items.a: We all agree with this plan.
wrong: We're all fed up with this plan.
We all made this plan together.

items.q: What does this sentence mean?
items.hi: ढीली रस्सी टूट गई ।
wrong: टूट गई is intransitive: it broke by itself.

items.q: What does this sentence mean?
items.hi: यह निहायत क़ीमती घड़ी है ।
items.a: This is an extremely valuable watch.

items.q: In an unfulfilled condition (अगर मैं अमीर होता …), the verbs are …
wrong: Future forms make an open condition.
A perfective in the अगर clause makes a supposition, and an auxiliary makes it a plain statement.
items.why: An unfulfilled, hypothetical condition uses the imperfective participle without an auxiliary in both clauses (अगर मैं कवि होता तो … लिखता). The feminine plural is nasalized. अगर is often dropped.

items.q: What does a perfective verb in the अगर clause (अगर मोहन आया …) suggest?
wrong: The perfective here isn't past: it treats the condition as a given.
That would be an unfulfilled condition, with आता.
items.why: A perfective verb in the अगर clause makes the condition a given, a supposition: अगर मोहन आया तो … “supposing Mohan comes …”.

items.q: A compound verb takes ने only when …
items.a: both the main verb and the auxiliary take ने
wrong: Both must: पी डाला takes ने, but कर बैठा doesn't.
Both must: करना takes ने, but कर बैठना doesn't.
items.why: A compound verb takes ने only when both the main verb and the auxiliary take ने.

items.q: Which auxiliary adds a sense of suddenness?
wrong: रखना suggests firmness or a lasting result.
items.why: पड़ना as an auxiliary: suddenness or a change of state, sometimes downward movement (रो पड़ना “burst into tears”, उतर पड़ना).

items.q: Which auxiliary suggests the start of an action or feeling?
wrong: रखना suggests firmness or a lasting result.
items.why: उठना as an auxiliary: the start of an action or feeling, sometimes upward movement (बिगड़ उठना “flare up”, जल उठना “burst into flames”).

items.q: Which word is the formal, Sanskritic one?
wrong: ज़रूरत is the everyday, Perso-Arabic word for “need”.
मुश्किल is the everyday word for “difficult”.
items.why: Formal Hindi uses many Sanskrit loanwords, everyday Hindi a freer mix with many Perso-Arabic words: समाप्त / ख़त्म, प्रश्न / सवाल, वर्ष / साल, यात्रा / सफ़र, उत्तर / जवाब, आवश्यकता / ज़रूरत.

items.q: हालाँकि “although” is usually answered in the second clause by …
items.why: हालाँकि “although” opens the first clause, and फिर भी or तो भी “even so” the second. Formal Hindi uses यद्यपि … तथापि.
